## Reading verification evidence

Verification asks whether the implementation solves its stated discrete problem. This chapter separates
an assertion in source, an independent algebra check and a measured execution of a pinned build.
A tolerance is an acceptance criterion; it is not an observed error.

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Interpret conservation residuals and convergence ratios.

**Data.** Cell averages, face fluxes and a named reference solution.

**Placement.** Analysis after a test, outside the solver step.

**Activation.** No solver switch; select a test and record its environment.

**Guarantee / limits.** Algebra checks do not execute a compiled solver.

**Evidence.** `metrics_check.py` checks every algebraic identity below.
:::

This is a selected catalogue, organized by the existing chapter entries. The generated test index in
@sec-appc provides a broader historical inventory; read its recorded provenance before using it at a new pin. A missing row here does not mean a test is absent.
The chapter adds no compiled CPU, CUDA or multi-rank results at the code pin.

Local symbols: $V_i$ is cell volume in $\mathrm{m^3}$, $A_{i\pm1/2}$ is face area in $\mathrm{m^2}$,
$\bar\rho_i$ is total density in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$ and $F_{i\pm1/2}$ is mass flux density in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$.
The oracle $\mathcal O$ has the units of the quantity being compared. The proposed local order symbols are defined below.

### Derivation

1. Multiply the divergence by cell volume before summing; otherwise adjacent face contributions do not cancel on unequal cells ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::divergence >}}).
2. Normalize by a nonzero reference only; the wall-saturation assertion uses initial energy and water totals ({{< code tests/test_wall_saturation.cpp WallSaturation.phase_change_preserves_energy_and_water >}}).
3. Infer order from a residual ratio only while the leading truncation term dominates; the wall test uses `log2(a / b)` ({{< code tests/test_wb_ref_wall.cpp faces_next_to_the_walls_are_second_order >}}).

#### Why a volume-weighted conservation check is necessary

Take a fixed, one-dimensional column with no mass source. Total density is $\rho$ in
$\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, velocity is $v_1$ in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, cell volume is $V_i$ in
$\mathrm{m^3}$ and face area is $A_{i\pm1/2}$ in $\mathrm{m^2}$.
With $\mathbf n$ the dimensionless outward unit normal, the continuity equation and its volume integral are

$$
\begin{aligned}
\partial_t\rho+\nabla\cdot(\rho\mathbf v)&=0,\\
\frac{d}{dt}\int_{V_i}\rho\,dV
  &=-\int_{\partial V_i}\rho\mathbf v\cdot\mathbf n\,dA.
\end{aligned}
$$

For a column, assume that the lateral boundary contributes
no mass flux. Let $F_{i\pm1/2}$ denote the numerical total-mass flux density in
$\mathrm{kg\,m^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$, oriented toward increasing $x_1$.
Replace each face integral by its area times the numerical face-average flux. With fixed volumes,
$\bar\rho_i$ is the stored density average and a dot denotes its semidiscrete time derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}
V_i\dot{\bar\rho}_i
 &=-A_{i+1/2}F_{i+1/2}+A_{i-1/2}F_{i-1/2},\\
\dot{\bar\rho}_i
 &=-\frac{\Delta_i[AF]}{V_i}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The positive face difference divided by volume is the operator in `CoordinateImpl::divergence`
({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::divergence >}}).
The statement here concerns that flux-form operator; it does not claim a particular reconstruction order.

Sum adjacent cells before evaluating a relative error. The upper-face contribution of one cell and the
lower-face contribution of its neighbour have the same area and flux and opposite signs:

$$
\begin{aligned}
V_i\dot{\bar\rho}_i+V_{i+1}\dot{\bar\rho}_{i+1}
 &= A_{i-1/2}F_{i-1/2}-A_{i+1/2}F_{i+1/2}\\
 &\qquad +A_{i+1/2}F_{i+1/2}-A_{i+3/2}F_{i+3/2},\\
 &= A_{i-1/2}F_{i-1/2}-A_{i+3/2}F_{i+3/2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Let $\mathcal I=\{1,\ldots,N\}$ denote all interior cells in the column. Repeating that cancellation over every internal face gives

$$
\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}V_i\dot{\bar\rho}_i=A_{1/2}F_{1/2}-A_{N+1/2}F_{N+1/2}.
$$ {#eq-ch15-budget}

The face differences in @eq-ch15-budget come from `CoordinateImpl::divergence`
({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::divergence >}}).
Thus the right-hand side is zero at closed walls. The identity is exact in real arithmetic if both cells use
the same face transfer. It does not hold by cancellation when the two blocks use different seam fluxes.
Floating-point sums can leave a residual. Summing density without volumes tests a different quantity on
an unequal-volume grid. The algebra check uses unequal volumes to expose that mistake.

#### A bound for the summation contribution

Assume round-to-nearest arithmetic, no overflow or underflow, and exact supplied cell masses.
Write the unit round-off as $\epsilon_{\mathrm{fp}}$ (dimensionless, local to this bound),
and the number of supplied masses as $N$. Each addition perturbs its exact result by a factor
$1+\delta$, with $|\delta|\leq\epsilon_{\mathrm{fp}}$. Expanding a sequential reduction gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\left|\operatorname{fl}\!\left(\sum_i V_i\bar\rho_i\right)-\sum_i V_i\bar\rho_i\right|
&\leq \left[(1+\epsilon_{\mathrm{fp}})^{N-1}-1\right]\sum_i|V_i\bar\rho_i|,\\
&\leq \frac{(N-1)\epsilon_{\mathrm{fp}}}{1-(N-1)\epsilon_{\mathrm{fp}}}\sum_i|V_i\bar\rho_i|,
\qquad (N-1)\epsilon_{\mathrm{fp}}<1.
\end{aligned}
$$

For the second inequality, expand the product and bound each binomial coefficient by $(N-1)^k$;
the resulting geometric series sums to the displayed fraction. Dividing this absolute bound by
$|\mathcal O|$ bounds the reduction's contribution to relative drift. Rounded products and an independently
rounded oracle add their own errors; flux evolution and division are not included in this reduction-only bound.
The `total` reduction in `WallSaturation.phase_change_preserves_energy_and_water`
({{< code tests/test_wall_saturation.cpp WallSaturation.phase_change_preserves_energy_and_water >}})
need not use sequential order, so this conservative bound is not a prediction of its observed residual.
It does not derive or replace the test's acceptance threshold.

#### Relative drift and a zero reference

Let $\mathcal O$ be the initial, nonzero mass oracle in kilograms. The relative drift can be written either
as a difference divided by the reference magnitude or as a ratio minus one:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\left|\frac{\sum_i V_i\bar\rho_i}{\mathcal O}-1\right|
 &=\left|\frac{\sum_i V_i\bar\rho_i-\mathcal O}{\mathcal O}\right|,\\
 &=\frac{\left|\sum_i V_i\bar\rho_i-\mathcal O\right|}{|\mathcal O|}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The same steps apply to a nonzero energy reference in joules or a water-mass reference in kilograms.
`WallSaturation.phase_change_preserves_energy_and_water` constructs volume-weighted totals and applies
this ratio form ({{< code tests/test_wall_saturation.cpp WallSaturation.phase_change_preserves_energy_and_water >}}).
For a zero reference the division is undefined. Use an explicitly chosen dimensional absolute tolerance;
do not infer one from a relative threshold. The catalogue keeps each test's own normalization.

#### What a two-grid order estimate means

Use a fixed physical domain and uniform cell width $h_i$ in metres. Let $\mathcal O$ now denote the exact
density oracle evaluated with the same averaging convention as $\bar\rho^{(h_i)}$.
The local symbols $\zeta_{15}$ (dimensionless convergence exponent) and $\psi_{15}>0$
(error coefficient, density units divided by $\mathrm m^{\zeta_{15}}$) are proposed additions, flagged in
`ISSUES.md`. They do not reuse $p$ (pressure), $e$ (specific internal energy) or $\mathcal E$ (energy functional).

Assume a nonzero leading error with a single power over the grids being compared:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert\bar\rho^{(h_i)}-\mathcal O\rVert_\infty&=\psi_{15}h_i^{\zeta_{15}},\\
\lVert\bar\rho^{(h_i/2)}-\mathcal O\rVert_\infty&=\psi_{15}(h_i/2)^{\zeta_{15}},\\
\frac{\lVert\bar\rho^{(h_i)}-\mathcal O\rVert_\infty}
 {\lVert\bar\rho^{(h_i/2)}-\mathcal O\rVert_\infty}
 &=\frac{\psi_{15}h_i^{\zeta_{15}}}{\psi_{15}h_i^{\zeta_{15}}2^{-\zeta_{15}}},\\
 &=2^{\zeta_{15}},\\
\log_2\!\left(
\frac{\lVert\bar\rho^{(h_i)}-\mathcal O\rVert_\infty}
 {\lVert\bar\rho^{(h_i/2)}-\mathcal O\rVert_\infty}\right)&=\zeta_{15}.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch15-order}

The same ratio applies to a nonzero scalar face error. `faces_next_to_the_walls_are_second_order` uses
`log2(a / b)` ({{< code tests/test_wb_ref_wall.cpp faces_next_to_the_walls_are_second_order >}}).
@eq-ch15-order is exact only under the single-power assumption. Higher-order terms, temporal error and
roundoff change the measured ratio. At least three resolutions give two adjacent ratios and allow a check
that the apparent order is stabilizing. Two grids provide one estimate, not proof of an asymptotic regime.

#### How to use

There is no simulation YAML for the symbolic metrics check. From the report directory, run:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python src/snapy_report/ch15/metrics_check.py
```

For solver evidence, use the named CTest registration in each catalogue section and record the build pin.
A zero oracle refuses a meaningful relative-drift interpretation; this is a mathematical precondition,
not a claim that the solver implements a new guard. In
`WallSaturation.phase_change_preserves_energy_and_water`
({{< code tests/test_wall_saturation.cpp WallSaturation.phase_change_preserves_energy_and_water >}}),
the mapping to the relative-drift identity is:

```cpp
double de = std::abs(total(IPR) / e0 - 1.);
```

Here `total(IPR)` is the volume-weighted energy and `e0` its initial reference.

[C2] The relative-drift identity assumes a nonzero positive oracle in the symbolic check.
[C3] The logarithmic order identity assumes a single nonzero power of grid width.
The new reduction bound is an analytic estimate, not an additional executed claim.[^ch15-metrics-run]

### Limits

Exact algebra cannot establish device parity, communication correctness, nonlinear stability or physical
validation. The catalogue states selected acceptance contracts, not an exhaustive coverage matrix.
The independent report checks can also fail because a stored output contains machine-dependent roundoff digits;
inspect the residual and its bound before interpreting that as a failed physical identity.
